children.description: A list of children the claimant is claiming for.

lives_with_claimant.description: Whether the child lives with the claimant.

in_approved_education.description: Whether the child is in approved education or training (e.g. A-levels, GCSEs, NVQ up to level 3). Only relevant for children aged 16-19.

in_extension_period.description: Whether the child (aged 16 or 17) has left education and registered with a government-sponsored careers service or the armed forces (qualifying for a 20-week extension).

upkeep_per_week.description: The amount in £ per week the claimant contributes towards the child's upkeep (food, clothes, pocket money, etc.). Only relevant if the child does not live with the claimant.

another_claimant_has_priority.description: Whether another person who also lives with the child has priority for claiming Child Benefit.

another_claimant_lives_with_child.description: Whether someone who lives with the child is already claiming Child Benefit for them.

care_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in local authority care.

care_home_24h_per_week.description: Whether the child spends at least 24 hours per week at home while in local authority care.

hospital_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in hospital or residential accommodation.

claimant_spends_on_child.description: Whether the claimant regularly spends money on the child (e.g. food, clothes, books) while the child is in hospital or residential accommodation.

is_fostered.description: Whether the child is fostered by the claimant.

council_pays_for_child.description: Whether the local council pays towards the child's accommodation or maintenance.

works_24_plus_hours.description: Whether the child works 24 or more hours per week in paid employment.

started_apprenticeship_in_england.description: Whether the child has started an apprenticeship in England.

receives_qualifying_benefits.description: Whether the child receives qualifying benefits in their own right, such as Universal Credit or Employment and Support Allowance.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text: I'd be happy to help you determine if you're eligible for Child Benefit! Let me start the assessment process.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Great! To begin, I need to understand your situation. 

**First question: How old is your child (or children)?**

The eligibility rules depend on the child's age:
- **Under 16**: Generally qualify automatically (with some conditions)
- **16-19**: May qualify if they're in approved education or training
- **20 or over**: Generally not eligible

Please tell me the age(s) of the child or children you're claiming for.

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Hi there! Thanks for helping me with this. I'm looking to claim Child Benefit for my son, Alex. He's 12 years old and lives with me at home.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information! So you're looking to claim Child Benefit for your son Alex, who is 12 years old.

Since Alex is under 16, let me continue with the assessment. Let me check the next step in the eligibility criteria.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
**Next question: Is Alex working less than 24 hours per week (or not in paid work)?**

Since Alex is only 12 years old, I would expect he's not working full-time, but I need to confirm this for the assessment. Is he:
- Not working at all, OR
- Working less than 24 hours per week?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, Alex doesn't work at all. He's just in school like any normal 12-year-old.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Perfect, that's what I expected! Let me continue with the assessment.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
**Next question: Is Alex NOT receiving certain benefits in his own right?**

Specifically, is he receiving any of the following benefits in his own name:
- Employment and Support Allowance (ESA)
- Universal Credit

Again, at 12 years old, this would be very unusual, but I need to confirm he's not receiving these benefits for the assessment to proceed.

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, he doesn't receive any benefits in his own name. He's just a regular 12-year-old - nothing like that applies to him.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Excellent, thank you for confirming. Let me continue with the next step.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
**Next question: Is Alex in any type of apprenticeship?**

This is about whether he's enrolled in:
- Any type of apprenticeship in England (Intermediate, Advanced, Higher, or Degree Apprenticeships)
- Modern Apprenticeships in Scotland
- Apprenticeships in Wales (except Foundation level)

Given that Alex is 12 years old and in regular school, I expect the answer is no, but I need to confirm this for the assessment.

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, of course not - he's only 12! He's just in regular school, not doing any apprenticeship or anything like that.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text: You're absolutely right! Let me continue with the assessment.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Now we need to check your residency status. 

**Question: Do you meet the UK residency requirements?**

You can qualify if ANY of the following applies to you:

1. **You normally live in the UK** (this is the most common scenario)
2. You have settled status under the EU Settlement Scheme
3. You have pre-settled status and meet certain conditions (working, studying, sufficient resources, etc.)
4. You're living abroad as a Crown servant or in certain qualifying countries

**Do you normally live in the UK?** This would be the typical situation for most claimants.

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, I live in the UK. I'm in Manchester with Alex.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Perfect! That satisfies the residency requirement. Let me continue with the assessment.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
**Next question: Are you responsible for Alex?**

You meet this requirement if ANY of the following applies:

1. **You live with Alex** (which you've already mentioned you do)
2. You contribute to Alex's upkeep by paying at least the same amount as Child Benefit towards his care (food, clothes, pocket money, housing, etc.)
3. You pay maintenance under a court order or agreement

Since you mentioned Alex lives with you at home in Manchester, it sounds like you do live with him. Can you confirm that?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, that's right - Alex lives at home with me here in Manchester.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Excellent! Let me continue with the next step.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
**Important question: Is anyone else currently claiming Child Benefit for Alex?**

For example:
- Alex's other parent
- Another relative or guardian
- Anyone else

Only one person can claim Child Benefit for the same child at a time. If someone else is claiming, you would need to arrange for them to transfer the claim to you, or HMRC would need to decide who has priority.

Is anyone else currently claiming Child Benefit for Alex?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, nobody else is claiming Child Benefit for him. It's just me and Alex, and I haven't claimed it yet - that's why I'm here asking about it now.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Perfect! That's good to know - so this would be a new claim and there's no one else claiming for Alex. Let me continue with the assessment.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
**Next question: What is Alex's current living situation?**

I need to check if any special circumstances apply:

- Is Alex currently **in hospital**?
- Is Alex currently **in local authority care**?
- Is Alex currently **fostered**?
- Or is Alex living normally at home with you?

From what you've told me, it sounds like Alex is living normally at home with you in Manchester. Is that correct?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, that's correct - Alex is just living normally at home with me. He's not in hospital, not in care, not fostered or anything like that. Just a regular home situation.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Great! Let me continue with the assessment.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
**Final question: Is the local council NOT paying towards Alex's accommodation or maintenance?**

In other words, are you covering all of Alex's living costs yourself (or with your family), without the local council paying for his accommodation or upkeep?

Generally, if the council is paying for a child's care, you cannot claim Child Benefit. But in a typical family situation like yours, this wouldn't apply.

Can you confirm the council is not paying towards Alex's costs?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: That's right - the council isn't paying anything towards Alex. I'm covering all his costs myself as his parent. It's just a normal family situation.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
## 🎉 Excellent News - You're ELIGIBLE for Child Benefit!

Based on the information you've provided, **you meet all the eligibility requirements** to claim Child Benefit for Alex.

### Why You're Eligible:

✅ **Alex qualifies as a child** - He's 12 years old (under 16)  
✅ **He's not working full-time** - Not working 24+ hours per week  
✅ **Not receiving disqualifying benefits** - Not claiming ESA or Universal Credit  
✅ **Not in a disqualifying apprenticeship** - He's in regular school  
✅ **You meet residency requirements** - You live in the UK (Manchester)  
✅ **You're responsible for Alex** - He lives with you at home  
✅ **No competing claims** - No one else is claiming for Alex  
✅ **Normal living situation** - Not in hospital, care, or fostering  
✅ **No council support** - Council isn't paying his costs  

### Next Steps to Claim:

1. **Apply online** at www.gov.uk/child-benefit or by post using form CH2
2. **Provide proof of identity** for yourself and Alex
3. **Provide Alex's birth certificate** or adoption certificate
4. **Payments**: You'll receive Child Benefit every 4 weeks (or weekly if you're a single parent or receiving certain benefits)

### Important Note - High Income Child Benefit Charge:

If you or your partner earn over £60,000 per year, you may need to pay back some or all of the Child Benefit through the High Income Child Benefit Charge. However, you can still claim and choose not to receive payments while still getting National Insurance credits.

**You can find more information and apply here:** https://www.gov.uk/child-benefit/how-to-claim

Is there anything else you'd like to know about claiming Child Benefit?

reasonings: Alex is eligible for Child Benefit because: (1) He is 12 years old, which is under 16 - meeting the age requirement; (2) He is not working 24+ hours per week; (3) He is not receiving benefits in his own right (ESA or Universal Credit); (4) He is not in a disqualifying apprenticeship; (5) The claimant normally lives in the UK (Manchester), meeting residency requirements; (6) The claimant lives with Alex, establishing responsibility; (7) No one else is claiming Child Benefit for Alex; (8) Alex is living normally at home (not in hospital, care, or fostered); (9) The local council is not paying towards Alex's accommodation or maintenance. All eligibility criteria have been met.
